daily.title: Poland: Thousands protest for more abortion rights
daily.summary: Thousands rallied across Poland to demand abortion rights six years after a landmark court ruling tightened restrictions. The country has one of the strictest abortion rules in all of Europe.

daily.title: Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
daily.summary: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

daily.title: Lina Attalah: Mada Masr journalist sent for trial in Egypt
daily.summary: Lina Attalah, who is accused of managing a website without a license, will go to court next week. Mada Masr has published reporting critical of Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi's government.

daily.title: 96% of world's coral reefs face critical risk of collapse, IUCN warns
daily.summary: Almost all of the world’s shallow-water coral reefs are at risk of collapse by 2075, with climate change the biggest threat. A new study found that 96% of reef systems are critically endangered.

daily.title: Canada's Mark Carney visits Turkey to boost trade ties
daily.summary: It's the first bilateral visit by a Canadian prime minister to Turkey. Canada and Turkey upgraded their relations to a "strategic partnership" as Canada seeks to diversify trade beyond the US.

daily.title: France's Macron says 'illegitimate' protests will be banned in coming days
daily.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron vowed to ban unauthorized protests after France was rocked by violence and looting. As anger over public services and the cost of living grows, authorities are bracing for more protests.

daily.title: Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
daily.summary: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

daily.title: Is Iran ready for another major US attack after midterm elections?
daily.summary: Iranian officials say the goal is to keep the regime in power and threaten enough regional costs to make a prolonged campaign unattractive. US media reports indicate that Trump is considering strikes after the midterms.

daily.title: Is EU putting profits over human rights in Vietnam?
daily.summary: The EU and Vietnam are deepening economic and diplomatic ties, but closer cooperation raises concerns about whether Brussels is doing enough to address Hanoi's human rights record, labor standards and trade imbalances.

daily.title: Germany news: Government expecting increased tax revenue in 2027
daily.summary: Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said state tax revenue will increase by €4 billion in 2027. Meanwhile, public service websites have been coming back online after a PHP security scare.

daily.title: India news: Gandhi's nephew forced to pull protest photos
daily.summary: The requested removal of "objectionable" photos from a cultural center took place in state run by Modi's BJP.

daily.title: France confirms first Shamonda virus infection in a human death of 'severely immunocompromised' individual
daily.summary: The Shamonda virus has been detected in a human for the first time, French health officials said. Authorities see no risk to the public, adding that the victim, who died in early October, was severely immunocompromised.

daily.title: Iran's Balochistan border region sees growing unrest
daily.summary: Violence is on the rise in Iran's border region with Afghanistan and Pakistan. The Iran war could shift the strategic balance for militant groups operating in the area.

daily.title: Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
daily.summary: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

daily.title: Germany arrests Ukrainian man suspected of spying for Russia
daily.summary: The suspect is thought to have gathered defense-related information on the production of tanks and munitions, as well as details about NATO's eastern flank.

daily.title: EU's Sakharov Prize won by the International Criminal Court
daily.summary: The EU has announced the International Criminal Court as the winner of this year's Sakharov Prize. The annual prize is awarded to individuals and organizations for their work in supporting human rights and democracy.

daily.title: Can Germany overhaul its economy before AfD grows stronger?
daily.summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Which new sectors could revive growth and contain the far-right AfD, whose support has grown larger than ever?

daily.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker?
daily.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is the clear front-runner for football's most prestigious individual prize, which will be awarded on Monday. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

daily.title: Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign
daily.summary: Bulgaria's presidential election campaign has been shaped by recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea and the government's reduced support for Ukraine, making foreign policy a key factor in the first round.

daily.title: Africa CDC calls crisis meeting as Ebola spreads
daily.summary: African health officials will hold a crisis meeting as the Ebola outbreak spreads from Congo to neighboring countries and beyond. The "extraordinary virtual meeting" will convene on October 28.

daily.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
daily.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

weekly.title: Germany news: AfD's Weidel calls for major EU reforms
weekly.summary: Far-right Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel reveals the party's plan to reform the EU. Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was in Berlin to talk to developers and investors. DW has more.

weekly.title: Trump, Putin and Xi at one table, without Ukraine. What Moscow wants from the proposal and why Beijing might agree.
weekly.summary: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, without Kyiv or the EU. What does Russia hope to gain, and why might China be willing to take part?

weekly.title: Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
weekly.summary: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity" between the two.

weekly.title: Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
weekly.summary: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.

weekly.title: Russia frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff talks
weekly.summary: During talks between Vladimir Putin and Steve Witkoff, Putin announced that jailed American Stephen Hubbard had been released. The Kremlin also said Russia was "in principle" ready to resume trilateral talks next month.

weekly.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
weekly.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

weekly.title: Football: German coach Hürzeler flying high in Premier League
weekly.summary: Fabian Hürzeler is younger than his star player, a fellow Premier League German. But, contrary to his reputation in his homeland, Hürzeler has become a popular figure both on and off the pitch in England.

weekly.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
weekly.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

weekly.title: UK fighter jets to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
weekly.summary: The UK is sending military support to Saudi Arabia as Iran-aligned Houthi rebels launch repeated attacks on the kingdom.

weekly.title: Portugal housing protests continue after police clear camps
weekly.summary: Demonstrators vow to continue their campaign to call for affordable housing in Portugal after police cleared tent camps and arrested at least 55 people.

weekly.title: New EU plan for Arctic warily eyes influence of Russia, US
weekly.summary: The EU unveiled its priorities in the Arctic as it vies with Russia, China and the US for influence. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said drone incursions, GPS jamming and cable sabotage undermine Arctic security.

weekly.title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
weekly.summary: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more news from Germany.

weekly.title: Wagner brothers begin new NBA chapter on different paths
weekly.summary: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new "German" team is the Charlotte Hornets.

weekly.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
weekly.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

weekly.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
weekly.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

weekly.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
weekly.summary: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

weekly.title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
weekly.summary: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.

weekly.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
weekly.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

weekly.title: What Earth's sixth mass extinction event means for humans
weekly.summary: Human activity is driving plants and animals to extinction at an unprecedented rate. As countries meet in Armenia to discuss ways to reverse nature loss, DW reveals how declining biodiversity is already harming people.

weekly.title: France: Young voters blase about Glucksmann's Socialists
weekly.summary: Raphael Glucksmann wants to lead France's Socialists to power without working with the left-populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, who is particularly popular with young voters. How can the center-left candidate win them over?

weekly.title: Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?
weekly.summary: Would you work 12 hours straight? The CDU/CSU and SPD are locked in a dispute over reforms to the Working Hours Act. Workplace flexibility, collective bargaining agreements and worker protection rules are at stake.

weekly.title: How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service?
weekly.summary: Kyiv keeps issuing warnings that the satellite internet system Starlink is being restricted in Ukraine. How dependent is the country on the system, and what would happen if it went down?

weekly.title: Populist Czech PM Babis goes empty-handed in Senate elections
weekly.summary: Opposition parties still control the Czech Senate, in a major blow to Prime Minister Andrej Babis' and his governing coalition.

weekly.title: How big is Russia's threat against Germany?
weekly.summary: Experts believe that, so far, Germany has been ill-prepared — both militarily and mentally — for Russian provocations. They also warn against the idea that ending support for Ukraine would make Germany safer.

weekly.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
weekly.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

weekly.title: Russia wants blackout in Ukraine as winter comes — Zelenskyy
weekly.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says Russia is trying to cut electricity and heating to civilians ahead of winter. He also called the US president's waiver of new sanctions on Moscow a boost for Vladimir Putin.

weekly.title: France: Protesters clash with police in nationwide protests, amid rising social polarization
weekly.summary: Unrest broke out in parts of France as students, trade unionists and Yellow Vest activists took to the streets to protest high prices and inequality. Police arrested over 1,000 people amid chaotic scenes.

weekly.title: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy speaks at EU summit amid spat with Donald Trump
weekly.summary: EU leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine at the Brussels summit. But souring relations with the US over Russia and Starlink and a big hole in the budget will make for a difficult winter for Ukraine.

weekly.title: Hijab ban at schools in Azerbaijan: What's behind the rare wave of protests?
weekly.summary: Girls wearing headscarves have been turned away from schools in Azerbaijan, triggering unusual protests involving children. The government rules do not mention hijabs. Why are schools enforcing unwritten rules?

weekly.title: The Bundestag has debated the genocide Germany carried out in Namibia a century ago. But will it spur progress on addressing colonial crimes?
weekly.summary: Opposition parties have forced a debate in the Bundestag on the early-20th-century genocide Germany carried out in Namibia. Will this finally spur progress in addressing colonial crimes?

weekly.title: Albania: Students demand political change and resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama
weekly.summary: Empty lecture halls, burning buildings and demands for change: Albanian students are spearheading a protest movement that has become the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Edi Rama in years.

weekly.title: The EU wants an AI revolution. But on whose terms?
weekly.summary: As the US and China race ahead, the European Union seeks to boost its economy with AI. Can it compete while protecting workers, safety and the climate?

weekly.title: Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue
weekly.summary: Citing problems with the data transmission network, Italian authorities have drastically reduced the volume of flights in their airspace. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.

weekly.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
weekly.summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

weekly.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
weekly.summary: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

weekly.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
weekly.summary: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
